source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    Check BMC could be update via serial port
1. Make the connection between serial port and client.Up
2. Use command to update BMC to newest version.
3. Restart the SUT and check the bios version.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria: 1. Make sure BMC could be update successfully.

deepseek_columns.ai_packages_needed: BMC image + serial cable/client (operator); bmcupdate tool
deepseek_columns.ai_commands: -- BMC update: updating the BMC via the serial port requires a physical serial connection to the client plus running the BMC update over that serial console; the agent cannot physically attach the serial cable.
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: operator connects the serial port, runs the BMC update to the newest version, restarts the SUT and checks the BMC version; agent cannot physically attach the serial link.
deepseek_columns.risk: RISK: BMC update over serial re-flashes BMC firmware; operator-only with the approved image, do not auto-run.

historical_reviews.deepseek: NO; identifies physical serial and BMC reflash risk, and silently corrects the source's BIOS-version check to BMC version.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: BLOCKED / CHANGED because target/artifacts/recovery were absent and BIOS-versus-BMC post-check conflicted.
historical_reviews.blocked_rereview_001: Kept BLOCKED with the post-check mismatch explicit.
historical_reviews.blocked_feedback_rereview_002: Changed to REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION; vendor inputs are readiness gates, while the BMC-versus-BIOS mismatch must be corrected.

original_test_intent: Update the exact platform BMC firmware through its approved serial-console path and verify the approved target BMC version, restored management connectivity, SEL/sensor health and host/platform recovery after restart.
original_method: An engineer establishes the validated serial path; after target/image/tool/recovery approval, the exact BMC update is executed and fully logged, the platform restarts as required, and the BMC—not BIOS—version plus management health is verified.
manual_activity: An engineer must attach/validate the physical serial path and supervise hardware recovery. After the exact plan is approved, update execution, transcript capture, restart/reconnect and electronic BMC verification can be automated.
required_inputs: Exact board/controller/current BMC and approved target version, not 'newest'
Signed BMC image/hash/release notes/compatibility and upgrade intent
Authoritative correction that post-update evidence targets BMC rather than BIOS
Stable power, maintenance window, credentials/config backup, recovery/reflash and alternate management path
safety_requirements: Do not flash while target identity, signature/hash, compatibility, serial path or recovery is unresolved.
Do not interrupt power/transport or assume current OOB remains available during BMC downtime.
Preserve baseline BMC/BIOS/SEL/network evidence and the full failure transcript.
Stop on mismatch, transfer error, management loss beyond plan, sensor/POST anomaly or unexpected settings change; never auto-retry.
agent_execution_scope: Inventory current controller/firmware/config/connectivity/sensors/SEL and validate supplied artifacts/tool plan.
After physical setup and approval, execute only the validated transaction with full transcript and downtime/reconnect timestamps.
Verify exact target BMC version, Web/Redfish/IPMI/serial reachability, sensors/SEL and host health; keep Tool Result separate.
engineer_actions: Resolve the post-check mismatch and approve the firmware manifest/serial/recovery plan.
Establish the physical serial connection and remain available for hardware recovery.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Correctly refuses to invent a command, but its evidence text silently changes BIOS to BMC. That correction requires owner authority and explicit SOURCE_CONFLICT tracking.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use only the owner/FAE-validated BMC updater and serial command; no generic replacement or guessed 'newest' target.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Serial update, restart, literal BIOS-version wording, BMC-success criterion and 10/5-minute fields are preserved; the mismatch is not silently rewritten.

modernized_recommendation.status: OWNER CORRECTION AND VENDOR PROCEDURE REQUIRED
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Bind controller/current-target BMC, signed image/hash, updater, serial settings, command/prompts, expected downtime and recovery in a manifest; after approved correction of the post-check, execute once and verify BMC version/connectivity/sensors/SEL plus host health.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Only the exact board/BMC/update path in the manifest.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Board/BMC vendor or FAE update/recovery documentation.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Makes the target/recovery explicit and corrects the erroneous BIOS check only with owner authority.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: No reduction; BIOS identity may be recorded for non-target-change comparison but cannot prove BMC success.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Owner semantic correction and complete vendor manifest.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: BMC flash can remove OOB management and reset configuration/sensors even if host boot remains available.

project_override_considerations: A project may approve an exact BMC target and corrected post-check. Missing artifacts are readiness gates, not permanent BLOCKED. The master source retains its literal BIOS wording and this conflict record; a project correction does not rewrite it.
expected_evidence: Controller/current-target manifest, signed image/hash, tool/serial parameters and owner correction
Complete update transcript/status and controlled restart/downtime/reconnect
Exact target BMC version and management/host health, non-target BIOS comparison, Tool Result and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The item, purpose and criterion require a BMC update, but step 3 explicitly says to check the BIOS version. BIOS version cannot establish BMC firmware success; owner correction is required and the source wording must remain preserved.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The intended BMC-update operation is clear despite the erroneous post-check, and the later re-review provides the safe correction path. Vendor artifacts are readiness gates; physical setup followed by automatable execution is PARTIAL rather than permanent BLOCKED.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Retain safety boundary but expose its silent semantic correction.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Retain all firmware safeguards and conflict finding, but reject permanent BLOCKED after the later readiness clarification.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Classifies the case as PARTIAL while separately recording the true SOURCE_CONFLICT and owner-decision requirement.

review_improvement: Avoids both unsafe generic flashing and false validation by BIOS version, while not treating supply of vendor artifacts as a permanent blocker.
independent_technical_reasoning: The BMC target is evident, so the bad BIOS post-check is a correctable field-level conflict rather than unknowable intent. Manual serial setup plus automatable validated flashing fits PARTIAL; formal evidence must target BMC firmware and health.
